33: A plot of land has the shape of a trapezoid. The bases $AB$ and $CD$ of this trapezoid have lengths $|AB| = 400$ m and $|CD| = 100$ m. The height of the trapezoid is 75 m, and its angles $DAB$ and $ABC$ are acute. From the plot, a rectangular parking area is to be marked out. Two of the vertices of this rectangle are to lie on base $AB$ of the trapezoid, and the other two - $E$ and $F$ - on legs $AD$ and $BC$ of the trapezoid [Figure: trapezoid ABCD with an inscribed rectangle AEFB shaded, E on AD, F on BC]. Determine the side lengths of the rectangle for which the area of the marked-out lot will be greatest. Determine this greatest area. Show your working. Hint: to relate the rectangle's dimensions, use that the area of trapezoid $ABCD$ equals the sum of the areas of trapezoids $ABFE$ and $EFCD$.
